_comment: Packages that may not enter this workspace, each with the ADR that forbids it.
A denied dependency is not a style preference — in each case adopting the package
would silently reverse a ratified architectural decision. Installing one is a
SUPERSESSION of its ADR, which is a reviewed decision, not a drift.
Checked by tools/check-dependency-denylist.mjs over every workspace package.json.

denied.reason: Replication-based sync bypasses RLS (ADR-0022) and moves per-user filtering into engine-side sync rules — a second authorization model beside scopeFilter(), which is C1 reborn at the sync layer.

ElectricSQL is the recorded ESCALATION path, not the starting point. Adopting it requires superseding ADR-0051, with shape definitions generated from the permission catalog so the second read-scope surface is derived rather than parallel.
Requires a zero-cache service and replaces the decided client data layer wholesale with ZQL (ADR-0050).
Drizzle is the decided ORM and its multi-schema proof of concept passed. Prisma is the recorded fallback ONLY if that PoC had failed; it did not.
PostgreSQL is the only datastore. A second datastore splits the transactional boundary that ADR-0004's modular monolith depends on.
PostgreSQL only. Queueing is graphile-worker (ADR-0027) on the same database, so a job and the transaction that created it commit together.
The Fastify adapter is the decision (~45k vs ~28k req/s for a one-line change). Installing the Express platform is how that reverts silently.

apps/web is a Vite SPA. ADR-0032 previously budgeted a Next.js standalone server at 512 MB against 2–4 GB of real need, on a box already committing 2 GB to Chromium — the inherited assumption this denylist entry prevents returning. A future customer portal is explicitly NOT covered by this: ADR-0050 scopes itself to apps/web.
